title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON SPECIAL MEASURES FOR RESTORATION OF HONOR OF PERSONS INVOLVED IN THE GEOCHANG INCIDENT, ETC.

ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON SPECIAL MEASURES FOR RESTORATION OF HONOR OF PERSONS INVOLVED IN THE GEOCHANG INCIDENT, ETC.

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Special Measures for Restoration of Honor of Persons Involved in the Geochang Incident, etc. and matters necessary for its enforcement. <Amended on July 2, 2019>

Article 2 (Organization and Operation of the Deliberation Committee for Restoration of Honor of Persons Involved in the Geochang Incident, etc.)
(1) The Deliberation Committee for Restoration of Honor of Persons Involved in the Geochang Incident, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the "Deliberation Committee") under Article 3 of the Act on Special Measures for Restoration of Honor of Persons Involved in the Geochang Incident, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") shall consist of the Prime Minister, who shall serve as chairperson, the Minister of the Interior and Safety, the Minister of Justice, the Minister of National Defense, the Minister of Government Legislation, five representatives of bereaved families commissioned by the Prime Minister, and one person with extensive knowledge and experience commissioned by the Prime Minister. <Amended on December 31, 2008; March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017; July 2, 2019>
(2) The five representatives of bereaved families who become members of the Deliberation Committee under paragraph (1) shall be commissioned for each incident to which the Act applies and shall attend meetings of the Deliberation Committee relating to the relevant incident.
(3) The Deliberation Committee shall have one executive secretary to handle its affairs, who shall be designated by the Minister of the Interior and Safety from among public officials belonging to the Senior Civil Service. <Amended on August 4, 2026>
(4) Deleted. <March 29, 2011>
(5) Deleted. <March 29, 2011>

Article 3 (Duties of the Chairperson, etc. of the Deliberation Committee)
(1) The chairperson of the Deliberation Committee shall represent the Deliberation Committee and exercise overall control over its affairs. <Amended on July 2, 2019>
(2) Where the chairperson is unable to perform duties for an unavoidable reason, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on the chairperson's behalf.
(3) The executive secretary shall handle the affairs of the Deliberation Committee under the direction of the chairperson and may attend and speak at its meetings.

Article 4 (Meetings of the Deliberation Committee)
(1) The chairperson of the Deliberation Committee shall convene and preside over its meetings.
(2) Meetings of the Deliberation Committee shall be convened with a majority of its incumbent members, including the chairperson, present, and resolutions shall be adopted with the affirmative votes of a majority of the members present. In such cases, members representing bereaved families who have not been commissioned in relation to the incident connected with the agenda of the relevant meeting shall not be included in the number of incumbent members.

Article 5
Deleted. <March 29, 2011>

Article 6 (Allowances, etc.)
Allowances and travel expenses may be paid, within budgetary limits, to members who are not public officials and to relevant experts who attend meetings of the Deliberation Committee.

Article 7 (Detailed Rules for Operation of the Deliberation Committee)
Except as provided in this Decree, matters necessary for the operation of the Deliberation Committee shall be determined by its chairperson following a resolution of the Deliberation Committee.

Article 8 (Organization and Operation of the Working Committee for Restoration of Honor of Persons Involved in the Geochang Incident, etc.)
(1) The Working Committee for Restoration of Honor of Persons Involved in the Geochang Incident, etc. under Article 4 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Working Committee") shall consist of the Mayor or Do Governor (hereinafter referred to as the "Mayor/Do Governor") of the relevant Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, or Do (hereinafter referred to as a "Si/Do"), who shall serve as chairperson; the administrative deputy mayor (referring to the First Administrative Deputy Mayor in the case of the Seoul Special Metropolitan City) or administrative deputy governor; and one deputy mayor of a Si, deputy head of a Gun, or deputy head of an autonomous Gu, four representatives of bereaved family members, and two persons with extensive knowledge and experience commissioned by the Mayor/Do Governor.
(2) The four representatives of bereaved family members who become members of the Working Committee under paragraph (1) shall be commissioned for each incident to which the Act applies and shall attend meetings of the Working Committee relating to that incident.
(3) The administrative deputy mayor or administrative deputy governor shall serve as vice-chairperson of the Working Committee.
(4) The Working Committee shall have one executive secretary and the necessary public officials to handle its affairs.
(5) The executive secretary shall be appointed by the chairperson of the Working Committee from among local public officials of Grade III or IV belonging to the relevant Si/Do.
(6) The public official positions in the Working Committee under paragraph (4) may be filled by public officials seconded from Sis, Guns, and autonomous Gus.

Article 9 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis)
Articles 3 through 7 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Working Committee. In such cases, "Deliberation Committee" shall be deemed "Working Committee", and "a member designated in advance by the chairperson" in Article 3 (2) shall be deemed "the vice-chairperson".

Article 10 (Registration of Bereaved Family Members)
(1) A person who intends to register as a bereaved family member under Article 7 of the Act shall submit to the Working Committee an application for registration of a bereaved family member in attached Form No. 1 (including an application in electronic form), attaching the following documents. In such cases, the Working Committee shall verify a certified copy of the resident registration record of the person seeking registration as a bereaved family member through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act and, where the applicant does not consent to such verification, shall require the applicant to attach it. <Amended on November 2, 2010>
1. A certificate of particulars recorded in the family relations records of the person seeking registration as a bereaved family member;
2. Written guarantees from three persons attesting to the fact that the deceased person died as a result of the Geochang Incident, etc. (limited to persons who resided in the relevant Eup, Myeon, or Dong at the time of the Geochang Incident, etc. and are at least 65 years of age as at the date of application).
(2) The chairperson of the Working Committee receiving an application for registration of a bereaved family member under paragraph (1) shall conduct necessary investigations into the qualifications of the guarantors, the contents of their guarantees, etc., and shall notify the chairperson of the Deliberation Committee of the application within 180 days from the closing date for registration of bereaved family members, attaching an opinion on whether the persons concerned qualify as a deceased person and bereaved family members. In such cases, where deemed necessary for the investigation, the chairperson of the Working Committee may request relevant institutions or organizations, including associations of bereaved family members, to state their opinions or submit necessary materials.

Article 11 (Fact-Finding Investigations by the Deliberation Committee, etc.)
(1) Before referring an application to the Deliberation Committee for deliberation, the chairperson of the Deliberation Committee who receives an application for registration of a bereaved family member and an opinion under Article 10 (2) shall conduct a fact-finding investigation into the particulars stated in the application and the required supporting documents. <Amended on January 5, 2021>
(2) Where deemed necessary for a fact-finding investigation under paragraph (1), the chairperson of the Deliberation Committee may request the heads of relevant institutions, organizations, or military units, relevant experts, residents of the area concerned, etc. to submit materials, provide other necessary information, or state their opinions.
(3) When the Deliberation Committee determines the deceased persons and bereaved family members, it shall register them without delay in the register of deceased persons and bereaved family members and notify the bereaved family members of that fact.

Article 12 (Procedures for Creation of Family Relations Registers)
(1) A person for whom a family relations register may be created under Article 6 of the Act shall be a person who died as a result of the Geochang Incident, etc. (hereinafter referred to as a "deceased person") and whose family relations register has not been created because the person was omitted from the relevant family register re-created after that register was destroyed in the Geochang Incident, etc., or because the relevant family register was not re-created.
(2) An application for creation of a family relations register under Article 6 of the Act shall be made by a person determined to be a bereaved family member under Article 11 (3) (where two or more persons have been determined to be bereaved family members of the deceased person, referring to the person having priority under Article 7 (2) of the Act).
(3) A person who intends to apply for creation of a family relations register shall submit an application for creation of a family relations register in attached Form No. 2 to the head of a Si, Gu, Eup, or Myeon handling affairs concerning registration of family relations under Article 3 of the Act on Registration of Family Relations (hereinafter referred to as the "head of a Si/Gu/Eup/Myeon").
(4) The following documents shall be attached to an application for creation of a family relations register under paragraph (3):
1. A certificate issued by the Deliberation Committee confirming that the person concerned is a deceased person;
2. A certificate issued by the Deliberation Committee confirming that the applicant is a person determined to be a bereaved family member. In such cases, where two or more persons have been determined to be bereaved family members, the certificate shall include confirmation that the applicant is the person having priority under Article 7 (2) of the Act.
(5) Upon accepting an application for creation of a family relations register under paragraph (3), the head of a Si/Gu/Eup/Myeon shall create the deceased person's family relations register and simultaneously close it.
(6) Matters concerning creation of a deceased person's family relations register that are not provided for in this Article shall follow the procedures prescribed in the Act on Registration of Family Relations and the Rules on Registration of Family Relations.

Article 13 (Detailed Rules for Implementation)
Matters necessary for the implementation of this Decree shall be prescribed by the chairperson of the Deliberation Committee.
